blocks.text: The challenge of API reference drafting

API documentation is not just prose. It is technical data that must be accurate, discoverable, and usable. When you are writing API documentation guides, you are essentially building a product for developers. If the code samples are wrong, the developer will fail. This creates a high level of pressure that does not exist in standard technical writing.
Why API documentation is hard to maintain

Most writers struggle because they try to write API docs like a user manual. Manuals are linear. APIs are non-linear. Developers jump to the endpoint they need. If your guide assumes they read the first ten pages, they will leave. Furthermore, the technical gap is real. You are often documenting code you did not write. If you lack a clear process, you will spend your day chasing subject matter experts for answers.

items: Organize by use case. Instead of listing endpoints, start with a goal like "How to authenticate a user."
Use a docs as code workflow. Keep your markdown files in the same repository as the code.
Test every sample. If you cannot run your own quickstart in under five minutes, rewrite it.
Use consistent naming. Ensure variables like maxPltCnt are expanded to readable names like maximumPalletCount.
Focus on edge cases. Developers care about error codes and rate limits more than the happy path.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive software to improve your workflow. Use tools that integrate well with macOS. iTerm2 is essential for running local API tests. Postman helps you verify endpoints before you write a single word of documentation. For capturing technical context, use Snagit to create clear diagrams or GIFs of your API responses.

faq.question: How do I start with docs as code?
faq.answer: Start by moving your documentation into your project repository as Markdown or MDX files. Use static site generators like Docusaurus or MkDocs to build your portal.

faq.question: Is AI useful for API documentation?
faq.answer: AI is great for drafting structure and basic descriptions, but it hallucinates technical details. Always verify every line of code it produces.
